subject: Routing exemption decision & customer comms handoff
messages:
From: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@acmecloud.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary routing exemption while we validate v2 model

Hannah,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap / ask from Acme's side: we’ve started sending production traffic to the new v2 chat model and are seeing a ~6% regression on a small set of high-value prompts tied to billing language. Our legal team is asking us to pause the automatic routing switch for our account while we run a 4–6 week QA pass.

Can Redwood enable a temporary routing exemption so Acme can continue to be routed to v1 for a limited window (we prefer 6 weeks but would accept 4) and then re-evaluate? We are OK with a conditional exception (monitoring hooks, a token cap) and happy to sign any exception form. I attached the initial exemption request PDF.

Attaching: routing_exemption_form.pdf

Requested next steps:
- Confirmation of whether Redwood can allow a per-account routing exemption and any constraints.
- If approved, a short comms note we can use internally for stakeholders.

Thanks,
Sam Ortiz
Senior PM, Platform Reliability
Acme Cloud

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary routing exemption while we validate v2 model

Team — looping you in. Acme (high-touch, enterprise) is requesting a per-account routing exemption to remain on v1 for a short window while they validate v2. They sent the exemption form and asked for comms we can share.

Context / constraints I care about:
- We should avoid a precedent that allows open-ended exemptions.
- We need guardrails (token caps, monitoring, expiry) if we allow it.
- Product needs to confirm whether routing-layer can enforce a per-account pin for the requested window without a service patch.

Can we converge on the below today so I can respond to the customer by EOD?
1) Policy recommendation: approve 4 weeks vs 6 weeks (we should default to shorter).
2) Technical constraints: max tokens/day, logging/alert hooks, auto-expiry date.
3) Billing/price implications: surcharge or discount?
4) Comms: clear one-paragraph note and acceptance form for Acme to sign.

I attached a draft comms note — please review and post quick replies inline. If this looks like it needs exec escalation, flag it.

Attaching: proposed_comm_draft.md

Thanks,
Hannah
Director, Customer Success (on behalf of Sales Ops)
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 10:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary routing exemption while we validate v2 model

On Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 11:03 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — looping you in. Acme (high-touch, enterprise) is requesting a per-account routing exemption to remain on v1 for a short window while they validate v2.

I scanned logs and did a quick impact assessment. My recommendation: approve a 4-week exception with the following mandatory conditions:
- Auto-expiry at 4 weeks (no manual extensions without an exec review)
- Daily token cap: 5M tokens/day on v1 for Acme; automatic throttling if exceeded
- Monitoring: set a regression alert tied to their key prompt set (INF-4821) and share read-only dashboard with Acme

Rishi / engineering notes?

—Marissa

---
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 10:45:00 -08:00
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Subject: Re: Request: temporary routing exemption while we validate v2 model

We can implement a per-account pin at the routing layer today via a flag; it would persist until TTL expiry. Effort: under a day to turn on with the following caveats:
- KV cache behavior: pinned routing will bypass multi-model batch optimizations and may increase cost by ~7–12% for those requests
- We should enforce the token cap server-side (easy) and generate an automatic alert to the Redwood Console if cap exceeded
- We need an audit entry created (who approved, expiry, link to exemption form) for compliance.

Ben: any billing concerns if we offer a one-time surcharge vs absorbing cost?

—Rishi

---
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:12:00 -08:00
To: all

I recommend we mark this as a paid exception: $Xk/month (covers the additional serving overhead and priority support). For negotiation, we can offer a one-time credit if they commit to a success plan post-exemption. Need to confirm exact number with finance; tentatively OK.

Karthik: if we approve, can you own cutover rollback plan and the quick re-route playbook?

—Ben

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@acmecloud.com>, Acme Cloud Legal <legal@acmecloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 15:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Approved: 4-week routing exemption for Acme Cloud (next steps)

Hi Sam — thanks for the patience while we evaluated this.

Decision (summary): Redwood will approve a time-limited routing exemption to keep Acme on v1 for 4 weeks, subject to the following conditions:
- Auto-expiry after 4 weeks from activation (no manual extensions without exec sign-off)
- Daily token cap: 5M tokens/day; automatic throttling if exceeded
- Monitoring: we will enable a shared read-only dashboard tied to the Acme prompt set and send alerts to your infra alias if regression thresholds breach
- Pricing: this will be a paid exception; our ops team will propose a one-time surcharge for the window (Ben will follow up with the exact amount).

Required customer actions:
1) Please sign and return the attached routing_exemption_form.pdf (it documents the expiry, cap, and acceptance of monitoring).
2) Confirm the primary infra contact for alerting and the acceptance of the daily token cap.

We will:
- Activate the pin at the routing layer once we receive the signed form and a confirmation of the infra contact. Rishi will turn on the flag and set the auto-ttl.
- Share the comms note for your internal stakeholders (attached draft).
- Provide a post-exemption review meeting slot in week 3 to discuss cutover plan and success criteria.

Attaching: routing_exemption_form.pdf; proposed_comm_draft.md

If this all looks good, please return the signed form by EOD Monday so we can schedule activation early next week.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
